prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate one finished full-fidelity desktop web app screen for the real product AI Benchmarks. Landscape target viewport 1440x1000; preserve this approximate 1.44:1 aspect, one screen only, straight-on screenshot with no browser or device frame. Surface structure in order: compact 64px top navigation, shallow 100px title region, horizontal benchmark tabs, huge white analytical plotting field occupying approximately 75% of the width, slim right-side model selector and evidence column, compact source notes and a 3-row result table beneath the graph, and a hint of the next model catalog section at the bottom. The visitor's job is to compare published AI benchmark score-versus-task-cost curves and inspect evidence. This is a premium Operate-mode research app, never a poster or marketing landing page.

Art direction "The research plate": luminous flat cool-blue page ground #edf2f8, pure white plot field, blue accent #3264d4, dark ink #172d46, subtle blue-gray rules. Geist/system-like clear modern sans, precise letter spacing, strong compact data hierarchy. Crisp high-fidelity semantic-style UI text and controls, generous data-chart whitespace, minimal 6px corner radii only on tiny controls. No nested card stacks, no large ornamental rounded panels, no shadows. No gradients, glow, photographs, fake logos, decorative illustrations, invented stat cards, testimonials, dates or commercial claims.

Navigation at top: left text wordmark "AI Benchmarks", then "Benchmarks" active, "Models", "Methodology"; small "GitHub ↗" on far right. Main content horizontal padding 56px. Title exactly "Intelligence, measured." around40px semibold and subtitle "Compare the latest models through published evidence." around16px, all inside the shallow title region.

Horizontal tabs across the top of the main workspace: "DeepSWE", "Terminal-Bench", "FrontierCode" active with a thin blue underline, "CursorBench", "Knowledge work". No vertical benchmark index. Below tabs the left analytical workspace is much larger than the slim right column. Left plot header "FrontierCode 1.1" 25px, small source line "Source: Anthropic", and understated segmented controls "Score vs. cost" active and "Results". Chart is the dominant visual, broad and professional. Plot thin straight line graphs connected point-to-point with small round markers; do not smooth the lines. Understated horizontal grid. Y-axis percentage ticks 30%,35%,40%,45%,50%,55%; use lower margin to accommodate29.2%. X-axis is logarithmic cost scale labelled $.25, $.50, $1, $2, $5, $10, $20; label "Task cost (USD · log scale)". Y-axis label "Score". Precisely approximate these score-cost series:
Sonnet5.5 blue #3264d4 at(cost,score) (.20,29.2),(.25,36.5),(.42,49.4),(1.59,52.1),(20.78,46.2).
Opus5.5 muted warm orange at(.41,47.3),(.82,54.6),(1.10,54.0),(2.24,51.4),(6.10,54.4).
GPT6Sol muted green/slate at(.43,37.3),(.76,45.9),(1.04,47.7),(1.33,48.4),(2.07,49.3).
These are design-preview pairs, not a universal model ranking. Elegant small line legend or direct series labels "Sonnet 5.5","Opus 5.5","GPT-6 Sol". Under graph exact note "Design preview · source values verified in build".

Right column aligned with the chart header: heading "Models" and rows with small square checkboxes. Checked rows and colored dots for "Opus 5.5","Sonnet 5.5","GPT-6 Sol". Other names "Fable","GPT-6.1 Sol","GPT-6 Astra","GPT-6 Luna","Grok 4.7","Kimi K3","GLM 5.3" have unchecked muted rows and small gray "Not reported" beside or below each. Keep all model names legible and spell accurately. Beneath a thin divider in this right column, concise evidence typography heading "Published evidence", text "Source-specific runs", short text "Evaluation conditions stay with each result." and a small source link "Anthropic ↗". Do not invent extra statistics or technical evaluation conditions.

Beneath graph, small source strip "Published results retain benchmark versions and source-specific conditions." and compact table with headers "Model","Effort","Score","Task cost". Three rows only: "Opus 5.5" | "Not labeled" | "54.6%" | "$0.82"; "Sonnet 5.5" | "Not labeled" | "52.1%" | "$1.59"; "GPT-6 Sol" | "Not labeled" | "49.3%" | "$2.07". Small label "Preview results" so this table is clearly a design preview. No invented confidence intervals, rankings or extra stats. At bottom show just the beginning of next section "Model catalog" with understated description "Explore models and available evidence.".
Everything should look like a real polished interactive research screen, chart-first, calm and airy, precise slim controls, restrained accessible navy text on blue-white surfaces.
